title: Newton's gravitation and Kepler's orbits
statement: Two bodies pull along the line between two centers; the inverse square law closes the orbit into a conic.
intuition: I let a small world fall around a star. A gentle change in eccentricity turns a circle into an ellipse.
source: MacTutor History of Mathematics archive; Kepler, Astronomia Nova; Newton, Principia
derivation: I combine the central force equation with angular momentum conservation; the radial equation has conic solutions and Kepler’s area law follows from the conserved moment.

title: Euler's identity
statement: The exponential map sends a turn through π in the complex plane to minus one, so the five basic constants meet in one line.
intuition: I draw a point walking around the unit circle. At half a turn, the point lands exactly opposite the start.
source: MacTutor History of Mathematics archive; Euler, Introductio in analysin infinitorum
derivation: I expand the complex exponential as a power series and set the angle to π; cosine gives −1, sine gives 0, and the identity closes.

title: The Hubble-Lemaître law
statement: At modest cosmological distance, recession velocity scales with distance through the Hubble constant.
intuition: I picture raisins moving apart in rising bread. Farther raisins separate faster because every patch of bread expands.
source: MacTutor History of Mathematics archive; Lemaître 1927; Hubble 1929
story: I put Lemaître's 1927 derivation beside Hubble's 1929 observations; the shared history deserves both names.
derivation: I write the scale factor as a(t), differentiate the physical distance, and read the local recession rate as H(t)d.

title: Planck's blackbody law
statement: Quantized oscillators give the spectral radiance of an ideal thermal emitter.
intuition: I turn a temperature dial and watch the brightest color move from red toward blue.
source: MacTutor History of Mathematics archive; Planck, On the theory of the energy distribution law
story: I keep Planck's reluctance in view. The quantum began as a mathematical move he did not trust, then remade physics.
derivation: I sum oscillator energies in discrete packets and divide the mode density by the Bose-Einstein occupation factor.

title: Laplace's tidal equations
statement: A rotating shallow ocean balances acceleration, Coriolis deflection, pressure, and friction.
intuition: I let a tide breathe across a rotating basin, then point toward the sister machine tide.jl.
source: MacTutor History of Mathematics archive; Laplace, Mécanique céleste
derivation: I depth-average the momentum equation on a rotating sphere, retain Coriolis terms, and couple velocity to surface height.

title: The Fourier series
formula: f(x) = a₀/2 + Σ(aₙ cos nx + bₙ sin nx)
statement: A periodic shape can be rebuilt from weighted sines and cosines.
intuition: I stack rotating arrows until a handful of circles draws a shape that looked too complicated at first.
source: MacTutor History of Mathematics archive; Fourier, Théorie analytique de la chaleur
derivation: I project a periodic function onto the orthogonal sine and cosine basis; the inner products become aₙ and bₙ.

title: Navier-Stokes
statement: Momentum, pressure, viscosity, and forcing govern a moving fluid; smooth existence in three dimensions remains open.
intuition: I send a stream around a stone. Small swirls carry a very large question.
source: Clay Mathematics Institute Millennium Prize Problems; MacTutor History of Mathematics archive
derivation: I balance material acceleration against pressure gradient, viscous diffusion, and forcing, then impose incompressibility.

title: The wave equation
statement: A disturbance on a string travels with a speed set by tension and density.
intuition: I pluck a string and watch one shape become a choir of harmonics.
source: MacTutor History of Mathematics archive; d'Alembert, Recherches sur la courbe que forme une corde tendue
derivation: I balance tension against transverse acceleration and take the continuum limit of a chain of small masses.

title: The Lorenz attractor
formula: ẋ = σ(y−x), ẏ = x(ρ−z)−y, ż = xy−βz
statement: Three coupled ordinary differential equations make a bounded flow that never settles into a repeating orbit.
intuition: I follow a warm current. A rounding choice can grow into a completely different weather story.
source: MacTutor History of Mathematics archive; Lorenz, Deterministic nonperiodic flow
story: I remember Lorenz's rounded printout and the butterfly effect without turning an anecdote into a myth. The equations do the work.
derivation: I reduce a convective fluid model to three coupled modes and integrate the resulting first-order system with a fixed-step method.

title: Maxwell's equations
statement: Electric and magnetic fields source, curl, and carry one another as a wave.
intuition: I drag a charge through a quiet field and let lines of force lean into motion.
source: MacTutor History of Mathematics archive; Maxwell, A Treatise on Electricity and Magnetism; Faraday
story: I put Faraday's field intuition next to Maxwell's equations. The mathematics did not erase the experiment that made it possible.
derivation: I collect the local electric and magnetic laws, then take a time derivative to reveal waves moving at 1 over the square root of μ₀ε₀.

title: Phyllotaxis and the golden angle
statement: A near irrational divergence angle spreads successive leaves and seeds across a disc with unusual evenness.
intuition: I place seeds one by one. At 137.5 degrees, no spoke forms and the spaces share the light.
source: MacTutor History of Mathematics archive; Vogel, A better photosynthetic solar energy collector
story: I credit the Indian mathematics carried west through Fibonacci's Liber Abaci, then name Kepler and Vogel where the botanical story continues.
derivation: I choose a divergence angle irrational relative to a full turn; the golden-angle limit spreads every new point across the available gaps.

title: Turing patterns
statement: Two reacting substances can destabilize a uniform field and grow spots, stripes, and labyrinths.
intuition: I seed a quiet skin with a tiny difference and let chemistry draw the pattern.
source: MacTutor History of Mathematics archive; Turing, The chemical basis of morphogenesis
derivation: I linearize two reaction-diffusion equations around a uniform state; unequal diffusion can make a finite spatial mode unstable.

title: Lotka-Volterra
formula: dx/dt = αx − βxy; dy/dt = δxy − γy
statement: Predator and prey populations trace coupled cycles when each population changes the other's rate.
intuition: I turn rabbits and foxes into a loop. Neither line owns the rhythm for long.
source: MacTutor History of Mathematics archive; Lotka, Elements of Physical Biology; Volterra
derivation: I multiply each population by its per-capita growth rate; interaction terms cancel into a conserved closed-orbit quantity.

title: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium
statement: With random mating and no evolutionary forces, allele frequencies stay fixed while genotype frequencies settle into a square.
intuition: I mix two alleles through a calm gene pool and watch the proportions hold still.
source: MacTutor History of Mathematics archive; Hardy, Mendelian proportions in a mixed population; Weinberg
story: I keep Hardy's remark about biology in its place and give Weinberg's independent 1908 result equal room.
derivation: I multiply allele frequencies for independent pairings; p plus q equals one and the genotype terms expand into the square.

title: Hodgkin-Huxley
statement: Gated ion currents explain how a membrane turns a push into an action potential.
intuition: I press a membrane past its threshold and watch voltage rise, peak, and return.
source: MacTutor History of Mathematics archive; Hodgkin and Huxley, A quantitative description of membrane current
derivation: I sum capacitive current and three conductance currents; voltage crosses threshold when inward sodium current wins the balance.

title: The Schrödinger equation
statement: A complex wavefunction evolves under a Hamiltonian and gives probabilities through its squared magnitude.
intuition: I send a packet toward a barrier. A small tail appears on the other side, even when a classical particle would turn back.
source: MacTutor History of Mathematics archive; Schrödinger, Quantisation as an eigenvalue problem
derivation: I apply the Hamiltonian as the generator of unitary time evolution; the norm of the wavefunction stays fixed.

title: Noether's theorem
statement: Every differentiable continuous symmetry of an action yields a conserved current.
intuition: I shift the clock, rotate the room, or slide the origin. A quantity stays faithful because the laws stayed the same.
source: MacTutor History of Mathematics archive; Noether, Invariante Variationsprobleme
story: I place Emmy Noether at the center. Her theorem quietly organizes modern physics, and her path through exclusion deserves more than a footnote.
derivation: I vary the action under a continuous symmetry; the boundary term vanishes on the equations of motion and leaves a conserved current.

title: Boltzmann's entropy
statement: Entropy counts compatible microscopic arrangements through the logarithm of the multiplicity.
intuition: I shake gas particles in a box. Ordered corners are rare; spread-out arrangements have more ways to happen.
source: MacTutor History of Mathematics archive; Boltzmann, Further studies on thermal equilibrium
story: I let the equation on Boltzmann's tombstone speak, while keeping the statistical argument and its historical resistance visible.
derivation: I count microscopic arrangements compatible with a macrostate; independent multiplicities multiply, so their logarithms add.

title: Shannon entropy
statement: Entropy measures the average surprise of a source in bits.
intuition: I give rare letters more surprise and common letters less. A message becomes a measured landscape.
source: MacTutor History of Mathematics archive; Shannon, A mathematical theory of communication
derivation: I require a continuous, additive measure of uncertainty; the resulting functional is the probability-weighted logarithm in bits.

title: The uncertainty principle
statement: Position and momentum spreads cannot both be made arbitrarily small for the same quantum state.
intuition: I squeeze a Gaussian in position. Its momentum spectrum opens wider to keep the product honest.
source: MacTutor History of Mathematics archive; Heisenberg, Über den anschaulichen Inhalt der quantentheoretischen Kinematik
derivation: I apply the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality to position and momentum operators; their commutator supplies the lower bound.

title: The Pythagorean theorem
statement: In a right triangle, the area of the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the other two square areas.
intuition: I cut and turn the squares until area leaves no room for argument.
source: MacTutor History of Mathematics archive; Babylonian tablets; Chinese gougu tradition
story: I name Pythagoras without pretending he owned an idea known in Babylon and expressed in the gougu theorem. The attribution stays plural.
derivation: I compare the area of a square built from four copies of the right triangle; the two decompositions leave a² plus b² equal to c².

title: Bayes' theorem
statement: A prior belief updates through the likelihood of new evidence and the evidence's total probability.
intuition: I start with a hunch, meet a piece of evidence, and let the numbers decide how much the hunch should move.
source: MacTutor History of Mathematics archive; Bayes essay; Price's posthumous publication
story: I keep Richard Price beside Bayes. Price edited and published the essay, and the usual shorthand should not make him disappear.
derivation: I write the joint probability as P(A and B) in two orders and divide by P(B) to update the prior.

title: The Riemann zeta function
statement: Analytic continuation and the zeta function's zeros encode the fine rhythm of prime numbers; the critical-line claim remains open.
intuition: I place the nontrivial zeros on the critical strip and ask whether every one keeps to the central line.
source: Clay Mathematics Institute Millennium Prize Problems; MacTutor History of Mathematics archive
derivation: I continue the Dirichlet series beyond its first half-plane and use the functional equation to reflect the nontrivial zeros into the critical strip.

title: The Gauss-Bonnet theorem
statement: Total Gaussian curvature, with boundary curvature when needed, equals a topological invariant.
intuition: I deform a surface like soft clay. The local hills move, but the total remembers the surface's holes.
source: MacTutor History of Mathematics archive; Gauss, Disquisitiones generales circa superficies curvas; Bonnet
derivation: I integrate local Gaussian curvature and use the boundary turning term; the result collapses to the Euler characteristic, a topological invariant.
